source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: In the lecture-notes skill, some work is done by its bundled scripts and some by the model's own judgment. Which task belongs to the scripts rather than to the model?

options.text: Pulling a frame out of an .mp4 video file at a specific timestamp
options.feedback: That is ordinary, mechanical software: give it a file and a time and it returns the same image every time. The model's share is deciding which moment matters and reading what the frame shows.

options.text: Working out what a speaker means by "look here" or "as you can see"
options.feedback: Resolving a vague phrase to the thing on screen takes judgment about context, which is the model's half of the pairing. No script can tell which slide "look here" points at.

options.text: Judging which moments in a session are worth a screenshot at all
options.feedback: Choosing what deserves a picture is an interpretive decision, so it sits on the model's side. The script only runs once a moment has been chosen for it.

options.text: Deciding whether the finished notes read as narrative or as expository prose
options.feedback: Style comes from the skill's written instructions and the model's reading of them -- that is the very instruction the class proposed rewording. Scripts do not weigh in on prose style.
